verdict.rationale: Sill's own docs say there is no account and no server, and that the screen and input travel only between your own devices. They also describe paired devices connecting on the local network: tapping the Mac pairs it by itself, sessions move onto your network automatically, and nearby devices can connect directly the way AirDrop does. missing for 10: explicit documentation of how the host is discovered on the LAN (it is only implied by 'Tap it' and the session switching to your network), and independent or hands-on corroboration beyond vendor docs.

support.subject: As a power user, my devices find the host on the local network and connect without an account or a vendor server in between

citations.quote: There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
Tap it, and the device pairs by itself, with no code, while your Mac is unlocked.
when you get home, the session moves to your network by itself.
Direct Wireless Connection lets an iPhone or iPad near your Mac connect without a shared Wi-Fi network, the way AirDrop does.
Each iPhone or iPad pairs with your Mac once. After that, only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.
